history.content:
My character: Rowan Garvey. A twenty-three-year-old human man with brown skin, unruly dark hair, and ink-stained fingers, wearing a carefully mended charcoal coat and the inherited Garvey signet. Newly arrived and unsure of Conclave customs. He grew up unaware of his heritage, lost his parents young, and does not know whether he has any magic.

Begin the story shortly before the welcome dinner, in my room at Garvey House. I play Rowan Garvey.

Late light catches on the brass rim of the Garvey signet where it rests against your mended charcoal cuff. The desk holds the framed letter from a dead aunt you never met, set beside a neat stack of Academy papers. New wool, lamp oil, and the faint mineral smell of rain from the gardens have settled into the room.

Below, chairs scrape over the dining-hall floor. Someone says something too low to make out; a quick laugh follows, then the solid clink of serving dishes.

A knock lands once on your door.

“Dinner is nearly served,” a woman says from the corridor.

Her voice is light and measured in short lines.

“Rashid has claimed the bread.
If you wait much longer,
he'll call it strategy.”

A beat passes.

“I am Seraphel Dawnquill.
I thought I could show you down.”

The corridor floorboard gives a small creak as she shifts her weight outside the door.
I open the door. "I would appreciate that. I'm Rowan." I follow Seraphel downstairs, greet the others at the table, and settle in to eat and listen.

Seraphel steps aside as the door opens. Her small white wings are folded close enough that only their tips show against her gold-and-white sleeves. At your introduction, her expression warms.

“Then welcome, Rowan Garvey.
I know the shortest route—
which is useful here.”

She takes you down a stair where old wood changes beneath the newer black stone of the lower hall. The common room opens past the landing: dead Garveys watch from their frames over a fire laid but unlit, and unfamiliar voices drift from the library doorway. Seraphel doesn't pause.

At the dining-hall threshold, six faces turn toward your greeting.

Rashid, with the promised bread basket within reach, lifts two fingers in answer. “You beat the soup. That's better than most first evenings.”

“Barely,” Ashara says from beside him. Heat gives the air around her a dry edge; her tail hooks around the back of her chair. “Sit before he starts counting it as a favor.”

Aldric rises long enough to incline his head. “Welcome to Garvey House.” Across from him, Ysolde studies you with a stillness that seems to leave room for the serving plates and nothing else.

You take the open place as a server sets a bowl of clear broth before you. Seraphel sits near Thessaly, who says, “It is a handsome house. It has too many stairs.”

Caelindra smooths one silver sleeve and looks from the signet to your place at the table. “The lawyers gave you an inventory, I assume. Did they explain which of the Garvey obligations are yours?”

provenance: Exact C8 session_b opening/turn1 replayed before player turn2; not a fresh independent story.
